title: the Atharva Veda's healing hymns
hook: one short hymn doesn't fight a cough. it gives it directions: fly off, as fast as a thought

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Atharva Veda's healing hymns came down to a pair of hands: one blessed, one more blessed still, with a touch that's kind. Whose hands did you notice? Day one thousand two hundred eighty-three.

Some ailments get a lecture. Some get a bargain. In one short Atharva Veda hymn, a cough gets something stranger: directions. Three verses, and in each one the speaker points the cough toward the horizon and tells it to go. Not to die. Not to be crushed. Just to leave, fast, and far. It's the kind of thing a person might mutter late at night, propped up on pillows, tired of the rattle in their chest. Except here it's poetry, and the poetry is all about speed and distance. Today: a cough sent flying.
screen: `A LECTURE, A BARGAIN, OR DIRECTIONS?` → `GO. FAST, AND FAR.`

segments.voice: Here is the hymn, in paraphrase. As the mind, with its wishes, flies swiftly far away, so, cough, fly off along the mind's own course. As a sharpened arrow flies swiftly far away, so, cough, fly off across the wide earth. As the rays of the sun fly swiftly far away, so, cough, fly off along the surge of the sea. That's the whole thing. Three pictures, and each one goes farther than the last. First the mind. Anyone whose thoughts have wandered off in the middle of a sentence knows how fast that is. The hymn borrows that speed and lends it to the cough. Then an arrow, something made by hands, sharpened, crossing open ground. Then sunlight, crossing the whole sea. Inside a person, then across the land, then out over the water. Notice the posture. The hymn doesn't rage at the cough. It gives it somewhere to go. That's a different move from fighting. To be plain: this is ancient prayer and poetry, not a treatment, and a cough that hangs on is a reason to see a doctor. But the hymn's shape is worth keeping. Some troubles, a worry, a grudge, a replayed conversation, don't leave when they're fought head on. Sometimes they need a direction. As fast as a thought. As straight as an arrow. As far as sunlight on the sea.
screen: `AS THE MIND FLIES, FLY OFF.` · `AS A SHARPENED ARROW FLIES.` · `AS THE SUN'S RAYS CROSS THE SEA.` · `GIVE IT A DIRECTION, NOT A FIGHT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: three breaths with somewhere to go. Choose one small thing you'd like to send off: a worry, a tight spot, a bad mood. On the first outbreath, let it go as far as a thought goes. On the second, as far as an arrow flies. On the third, as far as sunlight on the sea. Then sit with whatever is left, without pushing. If you pray, you can rest in prayer here. The bell holds the time.
The Atharva Veda's healing hymns. Today, one that sends a cough away along the mind's course, across the earth, and over the sea. Today's word.
screen: `THE ATHARVA VEDA'S HEALING HYMNS — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the Atharva Veda's healing hymns. Today, when something nags at you, try giving it a direction instead of a fight, one long breath out, toward the horizon. Day one thousand two hundred eighty-three.

howItsDone: Hymns like this one belong to the Atharva Veda's recited tradition, passed from teacher to student, and are read today as a window onto how ancient Vedic people spoke about illness and healing.
